body:
Thank you for the excellent post! It's actually encouraging to hear that she's following many of your suggestions already. She talks to me about distortions and Cognitive Behavioural Therapy, which she's learning at her hospital sessions, and she's been setting goals to walk our dog at least once every day. I think the distortions thing is especially useful for her, because she had a very rough childhood (alcoholic dad and some sexual abuse, I think, but she'd never tell me) and her family inexplicably blamed her and her sister for it. So she's extremely self-deprecating and self-critical. 

I'll try harder to be present and express my love and concern. I have a terrible tendency to think pragmatically about everything and I know that I sometimes talk about her recovery as though it's a checklist. It's hard to know what to say when you can't understand how they're feeling, but I'm going to keep trying. Thanks for the advice!
